Turn 1 of 4 — read-back. Do not write any program JSON in this turn.

You are going to turn a protocol into a Rhylthyme program: parallel **tracks** of sequential **steps**, each with a duration and a start trigger, that one person follows against a live clock.

Plan this as a Rhylthyme protocol and deliver a live timeline: Sandwich ELISA on Two Plates, One Washer for two 96-well plates, staggered 30 minutes
Resource limits: one plate washer, one 37 °C incubator holding two plates, one plate reader, one operator.
No finishing time was given; finish as early as the work allows.

Source text (read all of it):
<<<
Sandwich ELISA on Two Plates, One Washer

Two 96-well plates are run half an hour apart through a sandwich ELISA for a secreted cytokine. There is one automated plate washer, one 37 °C plate incubator that holds two plates, one plate reader and one operator. The washer is the bottleneck: no two plates can be in it at once, and every incubation is bracketed by a wash.

Day 1
1. Coat plate 1 with 100 µL per well of capture antibody in carbonate buffer, seal it and leave it in the cold room at 4 °C overnight. Take it out when you are ready to start, not before.
2. Coat plate 2 the same way half an hour later, so the two plates stay half an hour apart all day.

Day 2, reagents
3. Fifteen hours into the coat, make up the seven-point standard curve in assay diluent; 30 minutes.
4. Dilute the samples 1:4 into assay diluent and lay out the plate map; 30 minutes.

Day 2, plate 1
5. Wash the plate four times with 300 µL of wash buffer; 5 minutes on the washer.
6. Block with 200 µL per well of assay diluent for 1 hour at 37 °C.
7. Wash four times; 5 minutes on the washer.
8. Add 100 µL of standards and samples and incubate for 2 hours at 37 °C. Nothing goes on the plate until the dilutions are laid out.
9. Wash four times; 5 minutes on the washer.
10. Add 100 µL of biotinylated detection antibody and incubate for 1 hour at 37 °C.
11. Wash four times; 5 minutes on the washer.
12. Add 100 µL of TMB substrate, develop in the dark for exactly 15 minutes and stop with 50 µL of 2 N sulfuric acid.
13. Read the absorbance at 450 nm with a 570 nm reference; 5 minutes on the reader.

Day 2, plate 2
14. Wash plate 2 four times as soon as the washer is free; 5 minutes.
15. Block plate 2 with 200 µL of assay diluent for 1 hour at 37 °C.
16. Wash plate 2 again once plate 1 is off the washer; 5 minutes.
17. Add the standards and samples to plate 2 and incubate for 2 hours at 37 °C.
18. Wash plate 2; 5 minutes.
19. Add the detection antibody to plate 2 and incubate for 1 hour at 37 °C.
20. Wash plate 2 a final time; 5 minutes.
21. Develop plate 2 with TMB for exactly 15 minutes and stop it.
22. Read plate 2 at 450 nm; 5 minutes.
>>>

Read all of it before you answer. Then say back, in one paragraph and in your own words: what is being made, for how many (or at what scale), by when, and under what constraints — equipment that exists only once, how many people are working, anything that has to be held, rested or ready at a particular moment. If the text you were given looks truncated, or points at a section that is not here, say so instead of filling the gap.

End your reply with the same read-back as JSON in a single ```json fenced block:

```json
{
  "summary": "one paragraph: what is being made, for how many, by when, under what constraints",
  "servesOrScale": "8 people",
  "deadline": "2026-11-26T18:00:00",
  "constraints": ["one oven", "two burners", "two cooks"]
}
```

This is a two-plate sandwich ELISA for a secreted cytokine, scaled as two 96-well plates that are deliberately started 30 minutes apart; no calendar deadline is supplied, so the aim is to finish as early as the wet-work constraints allow. Day 1 consists of coating each plate with capture antibody in carbonate buffer, sealing it, and holding it overnight at 4 °C, with plate 2 coated half an hour after plate 1 so the two plates remain half an hour apart throughout the assay. Day 2 adds reagent-preparation work: seven-point standards and diluted samples/plate layout each require 30 minutes and must be ready before plate 1 receives standards and samples. Each plate then runs through repeated 5-minute washes, a 1-hour 37 °C block, a 2-hour 37 °C incubation, a 1-hour 37 °C detection-antibody incubation, exactly 15 minutes of dark TMB development stopped with sulfuric acid, and a 5-minute plate-reader measurement. The main constraints are that there is only one automated plate washer, so no two plates may occupy it simultaneously; one 37 °C incubator that can hold two plates; one plate reader; one operator; and a fixed 30-minute stagger between the plates, with overnight cold-room holding and the standards/samples prepared before plate incubation. The supplied text appears complete rather than truncated, though it intentionally gives no absolute finish time.

```json
{
  "summary": "A two-plate sandwich ELISA for a secreted cytokine is run on two 96-well plates staggered by 30 minutes, with no explicit calendar deadline and the goal of finishing as early as the protocol allows. Day 1 plates are coated and sealed overnight at 4 °C, with plate 2 coated 30 minutes after plate 1. Day 2 includes 30 minutes to prepare standards and 30 minutes to dilute samples and lay out the plate map before plates receive standards and samples. Each plate undergoes 5-minute washes bracketing incubations, a 1-hour 37 °C block, a 2-hour 37 °C incubation, a 1-hour detection-antibody incubation, exactly 15 minutes of dark TMB development stopped with acid, and a 5-minute absorbance read. The binding constraints are one automated plate washer that can handle only one plate at a time, one 37 °C incubator holding two plates, one plate reader, one operator, and the need to preserve the 30-minute offset between the two plates.",
  "servesOrScale": "two 96-well plates, staggered by 30 minutes",
  "deadline": null,
  "constraints": [
    "one automated plate washer",
    "no two plates in the washer at once",
    "one 37 °C plate incubator holding two plates",
    "one plate reader",
    "one operator",
    "two plates staggered by 30 minutes",
    "capture antibody coating overnight at 4 °C in sealed plates",
    "plate 2 coating starts 30 minutes after plate 1",
    "seven-point standards require 30 minutes before use",
    "samples require 30-minute dilution and plate layout before use",
    "standards and samples must be ready before plate incubation step 8",
    "every incubation is bracketed by a wash",
    "TMB development must be exactly 15 minutes in the dark",
    "TMB development is stopped with 2 N sulfuric acid before reading"
  ]
}
```

A track is one sequential lane of work, so steps inside it are chained and cannot overlap; if two activities happen at the same time, they need separate tracks. Each step has exactly one duration kind: `fixed` with `seconds`, `variable` with `minSeconds`/`maxSeconds`/`defaultSeconds`, or `indefinite` when it runs until the person ends it. A `startTrigger` places a step in time relative to the clock or another step using `programStart`, `programStartOffset`, `afterStep`, `afterStepWithBuffer`, `manual`, `onAbort`, or `compound`. `stepId`s are global, so the same id can never appear twice across all tracks, even if the step is conceptually similar on another plate. Every `task` claimed by a step must have a matching `resourceConstraints` entry, and that entry’s `maxConcurrent` controls whether two steps may use the same washer, incubator, reader, or operator at the same moment. Repeated work belongs on one step with `replicates: {count, mode, delay, maxInFlight}` and `instances: "each"`/`"all"` on downstream triggers, rather than duplicating steps or tracks unless the parallel work is genuinely separate.

Expected resource constraints:

- `operator`: 1 concurrent task, because there is only one person doing manual wet work.
- `washer`: 1 concurrent task, because there is one automated plate washer and no two plates may wash at once.
- `incubator`: 2 concurrent plates, because the 37 °C incubator holds two plates.
- `reader`: 1 concurrent plate, because there is one plate reader.
- `coldRoom`: 2 concurrent plates, because both sealed coated plates may need to be held overnight at 4 °C.

```json
{
  "acknowledgement": "tracks are sequential lines of work; one duration kind per step; triggers link steps; stepIds are global; every task needs a matching resourceConstraint with maxConcurrent; repeated work uses replicates with instances each/all and maxInFlight when a holding area limits in-flight work",
  "resourceConstraints": [
    { "task": "operator", "maxConcurrent": 1 },
    { "task": "washer", "maxConcurrent": 1 },
    { "task": "incubator", "maxConcurrent": 2 },
    { "task": "reader", "maxConcurrent": 1 },
    { "task": "coldRoom", "maxConcurrent": 2 }
  ],
  "actors": 1
}
```

Imagine you have to carry out this protocol yourself, in a lab where you have: one plate washer, one 37 °C incubator holding two plates, one plate reader, one operator, and everything must be ready at the earliest time the work allows. You have only the text below. Read all of it.

List every timed activity you would have to perform, in the order the text gives it, with:

- a short kebab-case `stepId` and a human `name`;
- `task`: the resource it occupies while it runs — the oven, a burner, the thermocycler, the PA, the bench, your own hands. Use the same name every time for the same resource;
- how long it takes: exact (`fixed`), a range (`variable`), or "until I decide" (`indefinite`);
- `sourceSpan`: the exact words in the text you took it from, as `{"quote": "...", "occurrence": n}`, where n says which occurrence of those words you mean (1 for the first). Quote the text verbatim — do not paraphrase it;
- `inferred`: `true` for a step the text never states but the work needs anyway (preheating, thawing, resting, cooling, labelling, sound-check), with `"sourceSpan": null`. Keep these few and obvious.

Split anything the text bundles into one sentence when the parts occupy different resources or different stretches of time ("brown the meat, then simmer for 40 minutes" is two activities). Do not decide yet which activities can overlap, which track they belong to, or what waits for what.
